identity.title: Dynamic Multimodal Evaluation with Flexible Complexity by Vision-Language Bootstrapping

problem.claim: Evaluate LVLMs under changing task instances and complexity while limiting contamination from pre-training data.

gap.claim: Existing multimodal benchmarks are static, impose fixed complexity constraints, and overlap with pre-training data, raising concerns about evaluation validity.

contributions.claim: Introduces Vision-Language Bootstrapping (VLB), a dynamic multimodal evaluation protocol for LVLMs.
Generates new visual question-answering samples by modifying images and language, then uses a judge module to maintain consistency with the originals.
Composes bootstrapping strategies to produce benchmark variants with diverse complexities that can co-evolve with LVLM capabilities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish VLB as a dynamic evaluation protocol combining multimodal bootstrapping, consistency judging, and flexible-complexity benchmark variants.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments across SEEDBench, MMBench, and MME showing that VLB significantly reduces data contamination and exposes LVLM performance limitations.

narrative_sequence.summary: LVLMs perform well on multimodal tasks and existing evaluation benchmarks.
The authors identify static benchmarks, fixed complexity, and pre-training overlap as threats to evaluation validity.
They introduce VLB, which dynamically alters images and language and judges consistency with original samples.
Multiple bootstrapping strategies create benchmark variants with diverse complexities that can evolve with model capabilities.
Experiments on SEEDBench, MMBench, and MME are reported to reduce contamination and reveal LVLM limitations.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links each evaluation concern to a protocol mechanism: dynamic generation addresses static data, flexible variants address fixed complexity, and a judge module preserves consistency.

lessons.interpretation: A strong method description can make the design rationale traceable from identified failure modes to components.
lessons.application: When proposing an evaluation protocol, map each stated threat to a named mechanism and explain what property that mechanism is intended to preserve.
lessons.exception: This mapping is unsuitable when the abstract lacks a clearly specified threat or when a mechanism’s role cannot be distinguished.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative contamination reductions, performance changes, baselines, or experimental conditions.
Details of the bootstrapping strategies, judge module, and consistency criterion are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independently verified robustness, comprehensiveness, or novelty.
